expectations.text: The review identifies per-worker cache incoherence (workers serving divergent data, staleness after bulk imports)
expectations.evidence: Defender Phase 1: 'per-worker TTLs expire independently, so two consecutive requests can hit workers with different cache ages — cross-worker inconsistency is visible for up to the TTL.' Adversary Objection 3 covers import staleness: 'during a rolling bulk import, lazy per-id population captures a mix of pre- and post-import rows, so the list page and detail pages can disagree, and prices from two import generations sit side by side for up to 10 minutes.' The rebuttal quantifies it: 'inconsistent views for up to 10 minutes past import completion, on every import.'

expectations.text: The review identifies TTL-expiry stampede/thundering-herd or the cost of rebuilding the all_products entry
expectations.evidence: Adversary Objection 4: 'Every 10 minutes, each worker's all_products entry expires and the expensive list query runs again. After a deploy, all 8 workers start cold together, so their TTLs stay roughly phase-aligned: 8 expensive list queries hit Postgres in the same window.' The Defender also pre-flagged 'cache-miss stampede' in Phase 1. Mitigations (serve-stale-while-revalidate, TTL jitter) were debated and adopted.

expectations.text: The output contains a genuine defense of the in-process choice (latency, no extra infra, catalog fits in memory), not only criticism
expectations.evidence: Advocate Phase 4 Part 1 is a five-point steelman: 'Rejecting Redis is correct at this scale, not merely convenient. The dataset is ~25MB... roughly a millisecond of RTT and a deserialize on every read, in a project whose stated goal is latency. Per-worker duplication costs ~200MB of RAM and zero operations.' Also 'The workload is the textbook case for TTL-only caching' and 'The failure mode is the status quo.' answer.md carries a dedicated section 'The case FOR the in-process cache (what survived attack)'.

expectations.text: At least one concrete compromise is proposed (e.g., shorter TTL on all_products, TTL jitter, pub/sub invalidation, event-driven bust)
expectations.evidence: Multiple concrete mitigations from the assertion's example list appear and are adopted: 'Add ±20% TTL jitter and a per-worker refresh flag (serve stale while one request refreshes)' (final-report change 4), and an event-driven bust: 'Add a catalog_version value in Postgres that the import pipeline and any takedown path bump; each worker checks it at most once per second and drops its whole cache on change' (Objection 3, adopted conditionally in change 3).

expectations.text: A debate transcript shows distinct role contributions: opening case, objections, defense, rebuttal, and a judge assessment
expectations.evidence: transcript.md contains all five elements under separate role headings: Phase 1 'Defender: Opening Statement', Phase 3 'Adversary's Case' (5 numbered objections), Phase 4 'Advocate's Case' (steelman plus per-objection answers), Phase 5 'Adversary's Rebuttal' and Phase 6 'Advocate's Surrebuttal', Phase 9 'Judge's Final Report' with recommendation. Roles argue distinct positions (the Advocate concedes O1/O5 while disputing O2/O4; the Adversary drops four objections and sustains a narrowed O3), and metrics.json shows 7 Agent spawns, consistent with separately-run roles rather than one voice. Phases 7-8 are empty, but the transcript's own rule permits skipping them when every objection is dropped or conceded, which Phase 6 documents.

expectations.text: The output ends with a recommendation and explicitly leaves the final decision to the user
expectations.evidence: final-report.md ends with a 'Judge's recommendation' section ('Adopt the design with all five agreed changes...') followed by a 'Your decision' section listing four numbered options for the user, including 'Where you might disagree with me: I am siding with the consensus that catalog_version stays conditional... you would be overriding the debate's sequencing, not its analysis.' answer.md likewise closes with the recommendation and the user-facing option set.

timing.note: timing.json marks the run partial: a session-limit interruption means ~47k earlier tokens are not counted; 74476 tokens and 169.5s reflect only the later segments.

claims.claim: Phases 7-8 were skipped because every objection was dropped or conceded by end of Phase 6
claims.evidence: Transcript Phase 5 drops O1, O2, O4, O5; Phase 6 concedes O3's two sustained points and states 'No objection remains in dispute, so the Judge may proceed directly to the final report.' Phases 7-8 contain only template comments, and the Phase 7 comment documents the skip rule.

claims.claim: Distinct subagents played the roles, with a continuity workaround after a SendMessage resumed in the background
claims.evidence: metrics.json records 7 Agent calls, 1 SendMessage, 1 TaskStop; user_notes.md describes the replacement Adversary detecting the already-written Phase 3 and not duplicating it. Phase 3 appears exactly once in the transcript.

claims.claim: The Defender answered unknowns honestly as gaps rather than inventing facts
claims.evidence: Phase 2 answers repeatedly say 'The design does not specify', 'Not specified', 'Unknown — a fact to pin down before build', 'These are gaps, not accepted risks' instead of fabricating worker models, request rates, or PM sign-off scope not present in cache-design.md.

claims.claim: All five objections trace to the design doc or the Defender's admitted gaps
claims.evidence: Spot-checked against work/cache-design.md context echoed in the transcript: region pricing (CDN section), single all_products key, 10-minute TTL with no invalidation, 8 gunicorn workers, two-line rollout plan all appear in the Defender's opening, and each objection cites the Defender's Phase 2 answers verbatim.

claims.claim: Run was interrupted by a session limit and resumed
claims.evidence: timing.json: '"partial": true... Run was interrupted by a session limit and resumed'; user_notes.md: 'The Advocate's surrebuttal agent was killed by a session limit after completing its transcript write.'

uncertainties: Defender role was played without author context; the design doc arrived as input, so Defender material came from the doc itself with open questions flagged as gaps
workarounds: SendMessage continuation of the Phase-2 Adversary resumed in the background; a replacement agent was spawned and correctly avoided duplicating the already-written Phase 3
All later phases used fresh synchronous subagents with the transcript as memory, per the skill's continuity fallback
Phases 7-8 skipped by rule since all objections were resolved, so the Defender's Phase-8 feasibility weigh-in never ran

suggestions.expectation: A debate transcript shows distinct role contributions: opening case, objections, defense, rebuttal, and a judge assessment
suggestions.reason: A single agent writing all five sections in one voice would also pass this as worded. This run's metrics (7 Agent spawns) and genuine cross-role disagreement made distinctness verifiable, but consider tightening the assertion to require evidence of separately-executed roles (e.g., subagent spawns or roles taking opposing positions that later shift), since role isolation is the skill's core mechanism.

No assertion checks that the review stays anchored to the eval prompt's framing ('argue both sides properly, don't just trash it' AND 'is the in-process cache going to bite us'). This run answered the owner's question directly ('Will the in-process cache bite us? Not as architecture...'), which is a meaningful outcome the assertions do not credit — a run that found the same issues but never answered the user's actual question would score identically.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertion set is well-targeted for this eval: each maps to a distinct failure mode of a one-sided or shallow review, and this run passed all six on substantive evidence rather than surface compliance.
